post.summary: Submit a Transport Order (Canonical Model) on behalf of the Shipper it names.
post.description: A booking that breaks Transport Order rules gets a 422 listing every reason. It is kept as Rejected, readable at the problem's instance. Submitting the same booking again (same Shipper, Shipper reference and content) gets a 200 with the original Transport Order, flagged as a repeat; reusing a Shipper reference for different content is rejected with ShipperReferenceReused.

get.summary: Count the Transport Orders received per UTC day, for the days from and to (both included).
get.description: A Rejected booking is not a Transport Order and is not counted. A day with none has no entry. The window is at most 92 days and is refused with a 400 when to is before from.

post.summary: Re-rate a Transport Order whose Rating failed, typically after its Rate Card was corrected.
post.description: Rates the order again with the Rate Card version valid on its collection date, and publishes TransportOrderRated or, when it fails again, another TransportOrderRatingFailed. An order that isn't Rating failed is refused with a 409 and left as it is: a Rated order's Freight Charge stays frozen. A re-rate sent again under its Idempotency-Key is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without rating again. Like the first rating, the re-rate continues the Message trail of the order's intake, so its event carries the intake's correlation ID, and a refusal's problem names it as correlationId.

post.summary: Assign an Accepted Transport Order to Own fleet or to a Carrier, which plans its one Shipment.
post.description: Creates the Transport Order's Shipment with a Shipment number and the status Planned, sets the Transport Order to Planned and publishes ShipmentPlanned on the Shipment events topic, all in one transaction. The assignment gets a new correlation ID, which ShipmentPlanned carries with the Transport Order number. An assignment sent again under its Idempotency-Key is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without planning again. An assignment that breaks an assignment rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: TransportOrderNotFound (404), TransportOrderNotAccepted or TransportOrderAlreadyPlanned (409), UnknownCarrier or InactiveCarrier (422). The rating result never blocks an assignment.

post.summary: Release a Delivered, Not yet billable Transport Order without a Proof of delivery.
post.description: Lets a Carrier that never sends a Proof of delivery not hold up billing for good. The remark and who releases it are required; otherwise the call is a 400. The TMS records who released it, when and the remark, and lifts only the NoProofOfDelivery blocking reason: an order that isn't Rated or has an open Exception stays Not yet billable. When the release completes the order, it becomes Billable and the TMS publishes one TransportOrderBillable with releasedWithoutProofOfDelivery set, in the same transaction, under a new correlation ID, which the answer and the event carry. The release publishes nothing of its own. A release that breaks a rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: TransportOrderNotFound (404), or AlreadyBillable, NotBilledSeparately, ShipmentNotDelivered or AlreadyReleased (409).

get.summary: Read a Transport Order or a Rejected booking by its ID.
List the rating exceptions: every Transport Order whose Rating failed, with its failure code and message.
List the Delivered Transport-only orders that aren't Billable yet, oldest delivery first, each with its blocking reasons.
get.description: Each order shows its number, Shipper, Shipper reference, when its Shipment was delivered and its blocking reasons: NotRated, NoProofOfDelivery and OpenException. A reason disappears when its condition is met, and an order that becomes Billable leaves the list. Orders whose Shipment isn't Delivered, Billable orders and Fulfilment orders aren't listed.

get.summary: List the Shipments to release: the Planned Shipments, with who carries each, in the order they were planned.
get.description: Each Shipment that came back from a Carrier booking shows its last one's outcome and reason, when it has one. A Carrier Shipment its Carrier's Carrier Rate Card can't price shows pricingFailure, with the code a release would be refused with (NoRateCard, NoValidRateCardVersion, NoMatchingLane or WeightAboveHighestBreak) and a message naming the Carrier: only such a Shipment can be released with a Spot price (P9).

get.summary: List the Released Own fleet Shipments not on a Trip yet, by collection time, optionally for one collection day.
get.description: Each Shipment shows its Shipper, where and when it collects and delivers, its weight and its pallets (P11). Pass day (yyyy-MM-dd) to keep the Shipments that collect that day, the date of the collection window's earliest time in Europe/Amsterdam. A Shipment leaves the list when it is put on a Trip.

get.summary: List the Requested Carrier bookings awaiting an answer, sorted by earliest collection time.
get.description: Each booking shows its Shipment, Carrier, Carrier booking number, requested time, sent time or none yet, and whether it is overdue: Requested longer than the TMS's setting, or past its Shipment's collection window's earliest time, whichever comes first. Overdue is only a flag; nothing acts on it.

get.summary: List the Shipments on their way: Booked, Collected and In transit, Stale ones first, then by ETA.
get.description: Each Shipment shows its number, who carries it, its status, its last Tracking event (type, time and place), or none yet, and its ETA: the last ETA a Carrier reported, or the delivery window's latest time when none did. A Stale Shipment, whose next expected Tracking event is late, is flagged and listed first, then the rest by ETA. A Delivered Shipment leaves the list.

get.summary: List the Delivered Shipments without a current Proof of delivery: flagged ones first, then the oldest delivered.
get.description: Each Shipment shows its number, who carries it, when it was delivered (the event time of its Delivered Tracking event), and whether its Proof of delivery is missing: the TMS's setting (48 hours by default) has passed since then. A Shipment leaves the list, and its flag clears, when a Proof of delivery arrives. Missing is only a flag; nothing acts on it and nothing is published.

get.summary: Read a Shipment's timeline: what the Carriers reported, and the Proofs of delivery that came in.
get.description: trackingEvents are in event-time order: each shows its type, time, place, ETA and remark, when the TMS received it, and whether it moved the Shipment's status. proofsOfDelivery are in delivery-time order, current and superseded: each shows who received, the delivery time, condition, remark and its files, which are read through the Proof of delivery file call, and whether it is the current one.

get.summary: Read a Shipment: its status, its Transport Order, who carries it, Own fleet or a Carrier, its history of assignments, and its Carrier bookings.

post.summary: Reassign a Planned Shipment to Own fleet or another Carrier, to fix a mistake before release.
post.description: The Shipment and its Shipment number stay the same. The TMS records the reassignment in the Shipment's history of assignments and publishes ShipmentReassigned on the Shipment events topic, with who carried it before, in one transaction. Each reassignment gets a new correlation ID, which ShipmentReassigned carries with the Transport Order number. A reassignment sent again under its Idempotency-Key is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without reassigning again. A reassignment that breaks an assignment rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ShipmentNotFound (404), ShipmentNotPlanned or AssignmentUnchanged (409), UnknownCarrier or InactiveCarrier (422).

post.summary: Release a Planned Shipment, handing it over to its Carrier (P4) or to Own fleet's Trips (P11).
post.description: The Shipment becomes Released, after which it can't be reassigned or released again. For a Carrier Shipment, the TMS also creates its Carrier booking, Requested, with a Carrier booking number. The TMS publishes ShipmentReleased on the Shipment events topic, with the Transport Order's addresses, windows and goods lines, who carries it, and the Carrier booking number for a Carrier Shipment, in one transaction. Each release gets a new correlation ID, which ShipmentReleased carries with the Transport Order number. A release sent again under its Idempotency-Key is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without releasing again. A release that breaks an assignment rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ShipmentNotFound (404), ShipmentNotPlanned (409), or, for a Carrier Shipment its Carrier's Carrier Rate Card can't price, NoRateCard, NoValidRateCardVersion, NoMatchingLane or WeightAboveHighestBreak (422), naming the Carrier, and creating no Carrier booking. A Carrier Shipment is priced at release, and its Carrier cost is frozen on the Carrier booking and carried by ShipmentReleased (P9).

post.summary: Release a Carrier Shipment its Carrier's Carrier Rate Card can't price, at a Spot price the Planner enters (P9).
post.description: The request carries the amount in EUR without VAT, in whole cents, and a required remark. The Carrier cost frozen on the new Carrier booking has one Freight line, the source Spot and the remark. It is otherwise a release (see ReleaseShipment), including its Idempotency-Key. A Spot price is allowed only when the Carrier Rate Card can't price the Shipment: it is refused with CarrierRateCardPricesShipment (409) when it can, and with SpotPriceNotAllowed (409) for Own fleet, creating and publishing nothing.

post.summary: Record the Carrier's confirmation or rejection of a Requested Carrier booking.
post.description: A confirmation carries the Carrier's own booking reference (required) and, optionally, a planned collection time: the booking becomes Confirmed and the Shipment Booked. A rejection carries a reason code (required, one of NoCapacity, LaneNotServed, WindowNotFeasible, GoodsNotAccepted, PriceNotAccepted or Other) and, for Other, a reason text (required): the booking becomes Rejected and the Shipment goes back to Planned. Either way, the matching event is published on the Shipment events topic in the same transaction; the Shipment's move publishes no event of its own. An answer sent again with the same outcome and content is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without recording anything again or publishing a new event. An answer is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: BookingNotFound (404, with that code) or BookingNotOpen (409, with that code) for a conflicting answer to a booking that already has one, ReferenceInUse (422, with that code) for a confirmation whose reference the Carrier already holds on another Confirmed Carrier booking, or the wrong Carrier answering (403, no code). A Carrier made inactive since the booking was sent can still answer it.

post.summary: Report that a Requested Carrier booking's request reached the Carrier.
post.description: Records the sent time on the booking and publishes nothing. A report for a booking that is no longer Requested (for example, withdrawn while the report was in flight) is ignored and logged: it changes nothing. BookingNotFound (404, with that code) for an unknown Carrier booking number.

post.summary: Report that a Requested Carrier booking's request never reached the Carrier, with its technical cause.
post.description: Moves the booking to NotDelivered and the Shipment back to Planned, and publishes CarrierBookingNotDelivered, in one transaction; the Shipment's move publishes no event of its own. A report for a booking that is no longer Requested (for example, withdrawn while the report was in flight) is ignored and logged: it changes and publishes nothing. BookingNotFound (404, with that code) for an unknown Carrier booking number.

post.summary: Report that the cancellation or withdrawal message for a Cancelled or Withdrawn Carrier booking reached the Carrier.
post.description: Records the Carrier told time on the booking and publishes nothing. A report for a booking that has already been reported told or not told is ignored and logged: it changes nothing. BookingNotFound (404, with that code) for an unknown Carrier booking number, BookingNotCancelled (409, with that code) for a booking that is neither Withdrawn nor Cancelled.

post.summary: Report that the cancellation or withdrawal message for a Cancelled or Withdrawn Carrier booking never reached the Carrier, with its technical cause.
post.description: Flags the booking Carrier not told with the technical cause and publishes CarrierCancellationNotDelivered, in one transaction. A report for a booking that has already been reported told or not told is ignored and logged: it changes and publishes nothing. BookingNotFound (404, with that code) for an unknown Carrier booking number, BookingNotCancelled (409, with that code) for a booking that is neither Withdrawn nor Cancelled.

post.summary: Withdraw a Requested Carrier booking before the Carrier answers.
post.description: Moves the booking to Withdrawn and the Shipment back to Planned, and publishes CarrierBookingWithdrawn, in one transaction; the Shipment's move publishes no event of its own. A later answer for it is refused with BookingNotOpen, and a later sent or not-delivered report for it is ignored. A withdrawal sent again under its Idempotency-Key is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without withdrawing again. A withdrawal that breaks the rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: BookingNotFound (404, with that code) or BookingNotOpen (409, with that code) for a booking that already has a different outcome.

post.summary: Record a Tracking event a Carrier or a Driver reported for a Shipment.
post.description: Takes only the Canonical Model. The event names its source: a Carrier ID (from API Management, never from the Carrier's payload) or Own fleet with the Driver ID (from the Driver's token, which the Driver reports Logic App passes on, never from the Driver app's payload). A Carrier's Shipment is the one on that Carrier's Confirmed Carrier booking with the Carrier booking reference. An Own fleet event names its Trip, the Shipment on it and the version of the Trip the Driver app held (kept for tracing only) in place of a booking reference, and the X-Correlation-ID is the Driver's action trail. A Driver reports Collected, CollectionFailed, Delivered, DeliveryFailed and Damaged. Collected and Delivered move the Shipment Dispatched, Collected, Delivered; CollectionFailed, DeliveryFailed and Damaged change no status and open the matching Exception (P7). Collected and Collection failed are the outcomes of the Shipment's collection Stop and Delivered and Delivery failed of its delivery Stop, each final on its Trip; Damaged is no outcome. The TMS stores the event with the correlation ID and the source's event ID. The Shipment's status only moves forward, and steps can be skipped: Collected moves it to Collected, Departed, Arrived and OutForDelivery to InTransit, Delivered to Delivered, publishing ShipmentCollected, ShipmentInTransit or ShipmentDelivered (only the one for the status landed on) in the same transaction. A late event, or one after Delivered, is stored and moves and publishes nothing. CollectionFailed, DeliveryFailed and Damaged are exceptions: stored, never moving the status, and published as ShipmentExceptionReported with the exception type and remark. The Carrier booking number finds the Shipment when no booking reference is given or it doesn't match. An event sent again under the same event ID is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without recording or publishing anything. An event is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says why: ShipmentNotFound (404), ShipmentNotInTransport (409), EventTimeInTheFuture, UnknownEventType or MissingRequiredField (400); and for an Own fleet event TripNotFound (404, also for another Driver's Trip), TripNotUnderWay, ShipmentNotOnTrip (checked against the Trip's latest version, even when the event names an older one), StopAlreadyCompleted (Damaged is exempt) or CollectionBeforeDelivery (409); and 400 for an input that isn't the Canonical Model.

post.summary: Record a Proof of delivery a Carrier or a Driver sent for a Shipment, with its files.
post.description: Multipart: the canonical metadata as JSON in the 'metadata' part and each file in a 'files' part. The metadata names its source: a Carrier ID (from API Management, never from the Carrier's payload) or Own fleet with the Driver ID (from the Driver's token, which the Driver reports Logic App passes on, never from the Driver app's payload). A Carrier's Shipment is the one on that Carrier's Confirmed Carrier booking with the Carrier booking reference. An Own fleet Proof of delivery (P12) names its Trip, the Shipment on it and the version of the Trip the Driver app held (kept for tracing only) in place of a booking reference, and the X-Correlation-ID is the one of the Delivered Tracking event it belongs to. The TMS keeps the files in its own storage, records the Proof of delivery as the Shipment's current one with the correlation ID, and publishes ProofOfDeliveryReceived in the same transaction as the record. A document ID the source already recorded is a repeat: the answer is the original result with isRepeat set, and nothing is recorded or published. A new document ID for a Shipment with a current Proof of delivery makes the new one current and supersedes the earlier, with nothing merged; the event says it replaces an earlier one. It never changes the Shipment's status. A Proof of delivery is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says why: ShipmentNotFound (404), ShipmentNotInTransport (409), MissingRequiredField (400), DeliveryTimeInTheFuture (400), FileNotAccepted (400); and for an Own fleet Proof of delivery TripNotFound (404, also for another Driver's Trip), TripNotUnderWay, ShipmentNotOnTrip (checked against the Trip's latest version, even when the report names an older one) or CollectionBeforeDelivery (409); and 400 for an input that isn't the Canonical Model.

get.summary: Read a Shipment's current Proof of delivery: who signed, when and where, the condition and its files.

Read one file of a Shipment's Proofs of delivery, current or superseded, with the content type it was sent with. A file the retention period has deleted is a 410 with the code ProofOfDeliveryFileExpired: the Proof of delivery and its file list stay.
List the Open Exceptions, oldest first.
get.description: Each Exception shows its Exception number, its Shipment, the Shipper, who carried the Shipment (Own fleet or the Carrier), its type, when it opened, how many causes it has, whether the Shipment was Delivered already when it opened and whether its cause is cleared. A resolved Exception leaves the list.

post.summary: Resolve an Open Exception with an outcome and a remark.
post.description: The outcome is one of NoActionNeeded, Redelivered, Replanned, ReturnedToShipper and ClaimHandledOutsideTms, and the remark is required; otherwise the call is a 400. The TMS records both and publishes ExceptionResolved on the Shipment events topic in one transaction, under a new correlation ID, which the answer and the event carry. The Exception leaves the list of Open Exceptions. A resolution that breaks a rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ExceptionNotFound (404) or ExceptionNotOpen (409).

post.summary: Add a note to an Open Exception.
post.description: The note is free text, so a phone call or an agreement made outside the TMS is on record, and both it and the Planner's name are required, and at most 2000 and 200 characters; otherwise the call is a 400. The TMS records the note with the Planner and the time, under a new correlation ID which the answer carries, and publishes nothing. The Exception stays Open, and the list of Open Exceptions returns its notes. A note that breaks a rule is refused, changing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ExceptionNotFound (404) or ExceptionNotOpen (409).

post.summary: Agree a delivery window for the Shipment of an Open Exception.
post.description: After agreeing a redelivery with the Carrier outside the TMS, the Planner sets the window on a Collected or In transit Shipment. Both its earliest and its latest time are required, and the earliest may not be after the latest; otherwise the call is a 400. The agreed window replaces the Transport Order's for Late delivery, Stale and the fallback ETA, while the Transport Order keeps the Shipper's window. The last one set counts, and earlier ones are kept. An Idempotency-Key is required: the same agreement sent again under it is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without agreeing or publishing again. An open Late delivery whose ETA is inside the window is marked cause cleared. The TMS publishes ShipmentDeliveryWindowAgreed on the Shipment events topic in one transaction, under a new correlation ID, which the answer and the event carry. An agreement that breaks a rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ExceptionNotFound (404), ExceptionNotOpen (409), ShipmentNotInTransport (409) or DeliveryWindowInvalid (400, for a window that ends in the past).

post.summary: Cancel the Confirmed Carrier booking of the Shipment of an Open Exception.
post.description: Before collection, the Planner cancels the Confirmed Carrier booking of a Booked Shipment when the Carrier won't make its collection. The reason is required, and at most 500 characters; otherwise the call is a 400. An Idempotency-Key is required: the same cancellation sent again under it is answered as before, flagged as a repeat, without cancelling or publishing again. In one transaction the Carrier booking becomes Cancelled, the Shipment goes back to Planned and the TMS publishes CarrierBookingCancelled on the Shipment events topic, under a new correlation ID, which the answer and the event carry. The Exception stays Open, and the Shipment returns to the Shipments to release as Cancelled by Norvia with the reason. A cancellation that breaks a rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ExceptionNotFound (404), ExceptionNotOpen (409), ShipmentAlreadyCollected (409) or NoConfirmedCarrierBooking (409).

get.summary: Get the message Notify Shipper starts with for the type of an Exception.
get.description: The template for the Exception's type, with the Shipper's reference of the Transport Order filled in. The Planner can edit it before notifying. ExceptionNotFound (404) for an unknown Exception number.

post.summary: Notify the Shipper from an Open Exception.
post.description: The Planner can notify the Shipper as often as needed while the Exception is open. The message, which starts from the template for the type, and the Planner's name are required, and at most 2000 and 200 characters; otherwise the call is a 400. The TMS records a Shipper notification with its notification ID and the status Requested and publishes ShipperNotificationRequested on the Shipment events topic in one transaction, under a new correlation ID, which the answer and the event carry. The Shipper notification Logic App reports it Sent or Not delivered. A notification that breaks a rule is refused, changing and publishing nothing, with a problem whose code says which, and whose correlationId names the Message trail the refusal is traced on: ExceptionNotFound (404) or ExceptionNotOpen (409).

get.summary: List the open days of the Planning horizon, one per day, earliest first.
get.description: The horizon job opens today and the next days at 00:00 Europe/Amsterdam (14 by default) and closes the days before today, which leave the list. Each day shows how many Vehicles are available and which Drivers work, with their Shift start and end and whether the Planner edited it by hand. It also shows the day's load check: capacity (available Vehicles paired with available Drivers) against demand (Planned and Released Own fleet Shipments collecting that day, Europe/Amsterdam) in kg and pallet places, and whether the day is Over capacity.

put.summary: Set one Driver's Shift on an open day.
put.description: start and end are required, otherwise the call is a 400. The Shift replaces the one from the Driver's Roster, or adds one on a day off, and is marked as edited by hand. A change that breaks a rule is refused, changing nothing, with a problem whose code says which: PlanningDayNotFound (404), DriverNotFound (404), DayClosed (409): days before today are closed and read-only, DriverAbsent (409): the Driver has an Absence that day, or ShiftInvalid (400): a Shift ends after it starts.

get.summary: List the Absences of today and later, earliest first.

post.summary: Record a Driver's Absence for one day or several.
post.description: id (the Driver), from, to (inclusive) and reason (Leave, Sickness or Training) are required; remark is free text. Days beyond the Planning horizon are accepted and take effect when the day opens. An Absence is accepted even when a Trip would use the Driver. Recording a day again changes its reason and remark. Refused, changing nothing, with a problem whose code says which: DriverNotFound (404), DayClosed (409), PeriodInvalid (400) or RemarkTooLong (400).

get.summary: List the Off the road days of today and later, earliest first.

post.summary: Take a Vehicle off the road for one day or several.
post.description: id (the Vehicle), from, to (inclusive) and reason (Maintenance or Repair) are required; remark is free text. Days beyond the Planning horizon are accepted and take effect when the day opens. Accepted even when a Trip would use the Vehicle. Refused, changing nothing, with a problem whose code says which: VehicleNotFound (404), DayClosed (409), PeriodInvalid (400) or RemarkTooLong (400).

get.summary: List each active Driver's Roster.

put.description: weekdays maps a weekday name (Monday to Sunday) to its Shift start and end; a weekday left out is a day off. The TMS rewrites every open day that isn't edited by hand and has no Absence; a day edited by hand keeps its Shift. A change that breaks a rule is refused, changing nothing, with a problem whose code says which: DriverNotFound (404) or ShiftInvalid (400).

delete.summary: Remove an Absence: the Driver works the Shift from their Roster again.
Remove an Off the road day: the Vehicle is available again.

get.summary: List the Trips of today and later, by day.
get.description: Each Trip shows its status (Draft or Dispatched), its day, and its Vehicle and Driver when it has them.

post.summary: Create a Draft Trip for an open day, with or without a Vehicle, Driver, planned start and planned driving duration.
post.description: Shipments to put on the Trip can be given as shipmentNumbers: they go on together or not at all, with the rules of adding Shipments to a Trip. day and an Idempotency-Key header (the same for each retry, which is answered with the Draft the first call created) are required, otherwise the call is a 400. A Vehicle or Driver given must pass P10's availability rules and have no other Trip that day, Drafts included. A request that breaks a rule is refused, creating nothing, with a 409 problem whose code names the first rule broken (VehicleNotAvailable, DriverNotAvailable, LicenceNotHeld, DayNotOpen, or for a Shipment ShipmentNotReleased, ShipmentOnAnotherTrip, CollectionDayMismatch, PayloadExceeded or PalletPlacesExceeded) and whose failures lists every rule broken. A plannedStart must be inside the Driver's Shift that day (OutsideShift), and a plannedDrivingDuration (more than nothing, at most 24 hours) must fit the Driver's Driving-hour budget (DrivingHoursExceeded).

get.summary: Show one Trip with its Stops in order, its load against the Vehicle's capacity, the rules it breaks now and its warnings.
get.description: Each Stop is derived from its Shipment: the collection or the delivery, its place, its window and its goods. The load counts the whole Trip as loaded at once. failures lists the rules the Trip breaks as it stands, such as a Vehicle that has since gone Off the road; warnings lists what doesn't stop it, such as a Shipment whose delivery window doesn't include the Trip's day. An unknown Trip is TripNotFound (404).

put.summary: Pick the Vehicle, Driver, planned start and planned driving duration of a Draft or Dispatched Trip. A Draft can give them back by leaving them out.
put.description: What is given replaces what the Draft had. A change that breaks a rule is refused, leaving the Trip as it was, with a problem whose code says which: VehicleNotAvailable, DriverNotAvailable, LicenceNotHeld, DrivingHoursExceeded, OutsideShift or DayNotOpen (409), TripUnderWay (409) for a Trip that is In progress, or TripNotFound (404). A change to a Dispatched Trip is an Amend: all four must stay given (TripIncomplete, 409), and a change that alters something raises the version and writes one TripDispatched under a new correlation ID, returned in the X-Correlation-ID response header.

delete.summary: Discard a Draft Trip, which gives its Vehicle and Driver back.
delete.description: A Dispatched Trip is never deleted: it is refused with TripNotDraft (409). An unknown Trip is TripNotFound (404).

post.summary: Put Shipments on a Draft or Dispatched Trip: each adds its collection Stop and its delivery Stop at the end of the sequence.
post.description: The Shipments go on together or not at all: the Trip is checked as it would become, and a refusal leaves it as it was. The load rules count the whole Trip as loaded at once. The problem's code names the first rule broken: ShipmentNotReleased, ShipmentOnAnotherTrip, CollectionDayMismatch, PayloadExceeded or PalletPlacesExceeded (409), ShipmentNotFound or TripNotFound (404), or TripUnderWay (409) for a Trip that is In progress; failures lists every rule broken. A Shipment whose delivery window doesn't include the Trip's day is accepted, with a warning. A Shipment already on the Trip stays where it is, so sending the same call again changes nothing. A Draft publishes nothing. On a Dispatched Trip this is an Amend: in the same transaction the version goes up, the added Shipments become Dispatched, and exactly one TripDispatched with the whole Trip is written to the outbox under a new correlation ID, which the X-Correlation-ID response header returns.

post.summary: Take a Shipment off its Trip until it is Collected, with a reason; it goes back to Planned.
post.description: In one transaction the Shipment's two Stops leave the Trip, the Shipment goes back to Planned (its Tracking status stays Scheduled) and exactly one ShipmentTakenOffTrip is written to the outbox for the Shipment events topic under a new correlation ID, returned in the answer and the X-Correlation-ID header. On a Dispatched Trip, also one that is In progress, this is an Amend too: the version goes up and a TripDispatched with the Shipments that remain, possibly none, is written under the same correlation ID. reason is required. Not idempotent: sending it again after it succeeded is refused with ShipmentNotOnTrip, since the Shipment has left. Refused with ShipmentCollected (409) once the Shipment is Collected, ShipmentNotOnTrip (409), VehicleOrDriverInactive (409) for a sent Trip whose Vehicle or Driver has gone inactive, TripNotFound or ShipmentNotFound (404).

put.summary: Put the Stops of a Draft or Dispatched Trip in order.
put.description: stops names every Stop of the Trip once, as a Shipment number and Collection or Delivery, in the order the Driver visits them. Two Stops at the same address stay two Stops. A Shipment's delivery before its collection is refused with CollectionBeforeDelivery (409), and an order that leaves out a Stop, repeats one or names another is StopsNotTheTripsStops (409); a refusal leaves the order as it was. Also TripUnderWay (409) for a Trip that is In progress, VehicleOrDriverInactive (409) for a Dispatched Trip whose Vehicle or Driver is no longer active, or TripNotFound (404). Sending the same order again changes nothing. A Draft publishes nothing. A new order on a Dispatched Trip is an Amend, which raises the version and writes one TripDispatched under a new correlation ID, returned in the X-Correlation-ID response header.

post.summary: Dispatch a Draft Trip to its Driver.
post.description: The Trip needs a Vehicle, a Driver, a planned start, a planned driving duration and at least one Shipment: each part it lacks is a TripIncomplete (409) and the Trip stays a Draft. Every Trip rule is checked again, so a Draft that became invalid, such as after an Absence was recorded on its Driver, is refused with that rule's code (DriverNotAvailable, VehicleNotAvailable, LicenceNotHeld, DrivingHoursExceeded, PayloadExceeded, PalletPlacesExceeded, DayNotOpen, OutsideShift, or for a Shipment ShipmentNotReleased, ShipmentOnAnotherTrip or CollectionDayMismatch), and nothing changes. On success, in one transaction, the Trip becomes Dispatched at version 1, its Shipments become Dispatched, and exactly one TripDispatched (version 1, the whole Trip with its Stops in order) is written to the outbox for the Trip events topic, under a new correlation ID that the answer returns. There is no event per Shipment. A Trip that is Dispatched already is TripNotDraft (409), not a repeat: the caller is the TMS UI, which doesn't retry a Dispatch, and a later version goes out by Amend or by sending the version again; an unknown Trip is TripNotFound (404).

post.summary: Send a Not delivered version of a Trip to the Driver app again.
post.description: Only the Trip's latest version can be sent again, and only while it is Not delivered. The version is Sending once more, and, in one transaction, exactly one TripDispatched with the same version and the whole Trip as it stands now is written to the outbox for the Trip events topic, under a new correlation ID that the answer returns. NothingToSendAgain (409) for a version that is Sending or Delivered, TripVersionNotLatest (409) for an older version, TripNotDispatched (409) for a Draft, VehicleOrDriverInactive (409) when the Trip's Vehicle or Driver is no longer active, TripVersionNotFound or TripNotFound (404).

post.summary: Report that the Driver app accepted a version of a Trip.
post.description: Sets the version's delivery state to Delivered to Driver app and publishes nothing. A report for a version that is no longer Sending (a repeat, or one that arrives after the other report) is ignored and logged: it changes and publishes nothing. A report for a version older than the Trip's latest is stored against that version and changes nothing else. The X-Correlation-ID is the correlation ID of the Dispatch or send-again, which the TripDispatched event carried. TripNotFound or TripVersionNotFound (404, with that code).

post.summary: Report that a version of a Trip never reached the Driver app, with its technical cause.
post.description: Sets the version's delivery state to Not delivered with the cause and, for the Trip's latest version, publishes TripNotDelivered in the same transaction. A report for a version older than the Trip's latest is stored against that version and publishes nothing. A report for a version that is no longer Sending is ignored and logged: it changes and publishes nothing. The X-Correlation-ID is the correlation ID of the Dispatch or send-again, which the TripDispatched event carried. TripNotFound or TripVersionNotFound (404, with that code).

post.summary: Start a Dispatched Trip on its day: the Driver reports it from the Driver app.
post.description: driverId is the Driver ID from the Driver's token, which the Driver reports Logic App passes on, and the X-Correlation-ID is the Driver's action trail. driverAppEventId, when it is sent, is the ID of the Driver app event: a Start that repeats the event that started the Trip is answered 200 with repeat true, and changes and publishes nothing. In one transaction the Trip becomes In progress, at the same version, and exactly one TripStarted (Trip number, version, Driver ID, start time) is written to the outbox for the Trip events topic under that correlation ID. From then on the only change the Planner can make is taking off a Shipment that isn't collected: every other change is TripUnderWay (409). Refused with TripNotFound (404) for an unknown Trip, or one whose Driver is not the Driver from the token, TripNotDispatched (409) for a Draft or a Trip that is In progress already, and NotTripDay (409) when today is not the Trip's day in Norvia's time.

post.summary: End an In progress Trip once every Stop has an outcome: the Driver reports it from the Driver app.
post.description: driverId is the Driver ID from the Driver's token, which the Driver reports Logic App passes on, and the X-Correlation-ID is the Driver's action trail. In one transaction the Trip becomes Completed, at the same version, and exactly one TripCompleted (Trip number, version, Driver ID, end time and the Shipments delivered, not delivered and not collected) is written to the outbox for the Trip events topic under that correlation ID. A Shipment that wasn't collected is Planned again and one that was collected but not delivered is flagged Awaiting re-delivery, keeping its status; both leave the Trip, and no ShipmentTakenOffTrip is published. Refused with TripNotFound (404) for an unknown Trip, or one whose Driver is not the Driver from the token, TripNotUnderWay (409) for a Trip that isn't In progress, and StopsOpen (409) while a Stop has no outcome. A refusal changes nothing.

post.summary: Report that a Requested Shipper notification was acknowledged by the Shipper's endpoint.
post.description: Moves the notification to Sent, records the time and publishes nothing. A report for a notification that is no longer Requested (a repeat, or one that arrives after the other report) is ignored and logged: it changes and publishes nothing. The X-Correlation-ID is the correlation ID of the Planner's action, which the ShipperNotificationRequested event carried. ShipperNotificationNotFound (404, with that code) for an unknown notification ID.

post.summary: Report that a Requested Shipper notification never reached the Shipper, with its technical cause.
post.description: Moves the notification to Not delivered with the technical cause and publishes ShipperNotificationNotDelivered, in one transaction. A report for a notification that is no longer Requested is ignored and logged: it changes and publishes nothing. ShipperNotificationNotFound (404, with that code) for an unknown notification ID.

get.summary: List a Shipper's Transport Orders with their Tracking status (Canonical Model), newest collection first.
get.description: Scoped to the Shipper in X-Shipper-ID, which is required, as is X-Correlation-ID; otherwise the call is a 400. Each item has the Transport Order number, the Shipper reference, the collection and delivery places, the Tracking status (Received, Scheduled, Collected, InTransit or Delivered), the ETA and the last update. The Tracking status is worked out when the call is made. It can be narrowed with trackingStatus and a collectionFrom to collectionTo date range (both ends included, by the date the collection window opens), and is paged with page (from 1) and pageSize (1 to 100, 25 by default), always newest collection first. Rejected bookings are not returned. Nothing in the answer names a Carrier, a Shipment number, an Exception or Stale.

get.summary: Find one of a Shipper's Transport Orders by the Shipper's own reference, with its tracking (Canonical Model).
get.description: As the get operation, which it answers the same as. Scoped to the Shipper in X-Shipper-ID; the reference is unique per Shipper. A reference that is unknown or another Shipper's is a 404 with the code TransportOrderNotFound, the same for both.

get.summary: Get one of a Shipper's Transport Orders by Norvia's number, with its tracking (Canonical Model).
get.description: Scoped to the Shipper in X-Shipper-ID, which is required, as is X-Correlation-ID; otherwise the call is a 400. Returns the collection and delivery places, the collection window, the delivery window (the agreed one when there is one), the Tracking status, the ETA, the last update and the progress: only progress Tracking events, in event-time order, without remarks. A Transport Order that is unknown or another Shipper's is a 404 with the code TransportOrderNotFound, the same for both. Nothing in the answer names a Carrier, a Shipment number, an Exception or Stale.

get.summary: Read one file of a Shipper's Transport Order's current Proof of delivery, streamed with the content type it was sent with.
get.description: Scoped to the Shipper in X-Shipper-ID, which is required, as is X-Correlation-ID; otherwise the call is a 400. A Transport Order that is unknown or another Shipper's is a 404 with the code TransportOrderNotFound. A file of a superseded Proof of delivery, a Transport Order with no Proof of delivery or a file it doesn't hold is a 404 with the code ProofOfDeliveryNotFound. P6's Planner operation to read a Proof of delivery file is unchanged.

get.summary: Read a Rejected booking as the Customer service agent: reasons and submitted content, without the Consignee's details.
Read a Transport Order as the Customer service agent: status, rating result, Shipment status and billing state with its blocking reasons.
Read a Shipment's Tracking events as the Customer service agent, with their sources and without the remarks reporters typed.
Read a Shipment's Exceptions as the Customer service agent: type, causes, status, the Planner's notes and whether the Shipper was notified.
Read where a Shipment stands for its Proof of delivery: current, superseded, missing, reservations. Never who signed and never a file.
Read whether a Transport Order may be released without a Proof of delivery, as the Customer service agent: the TMS's answer and, if not, every reason that blocks it.
Read what the Shipper sees of a Transport Order, as the Customer service reply agent: Tracking status, progress, Proof of delivery availability and the Shipper notifications already sent.
Read where a Transport Order can go, as the Planner agent: whether Own fleet fits, and each active Carrier's Carrier cost or why it cannot be priced, with the Assignment rules each meets.

As the assignment options, with the what-if tally of a plan of the waiting list: alreadyAssumed is the comma-separated numbers of the Transport Orders already suggested for Own fleet, which Own fleet's load check counts too. Nothing is assigned.

Read an Exception's timeline as the Planner agent, to draft an internal note: its type and cause, status, the Shipment's Tracking events with their sources, the Carrier booking's state, the actions already taken and the notes so far. No Consignee personal data and no file contents.
Read the message Notify Shipper starts with for an Exception's type, as the Planner notification agent. Only the template's words: no Carrier, no remark and no Exception details.
Read what the Shipper sees of a Transport Order, as the Planner notification agent: Tracking status, progress, Proof of delivery availability and the Shipper notifications already sent.

put.summary: Replace the TMS's copy of a Shipper with the ERP's record.
put.description: Upserts the whole Shipper, so a new Shipper appears. Idempotent on the Master-data revision: a revision that is not higher than the copy's answers 200 with applied false and changes nothing. The TMS never edits a Shipper itself. A record the TMS can't read (no name, a revision below 1) is refused with 400 and the code MasterDataUnreadable.

put.summary: Replace the TMS's copy of a Carrier with the ERP's record.
put.description: Upserts the whole Carrier, so a new Carrier appears. Idempotent on the Master-data revision: a revision that is not higher than the copy's answers 200 with applied false and changes nothing. The TMS never edits a Carrier itself. A record the TMS can't read (no name, a revision below 1) is refused with 400 and the code MasterDataUnreadable.

put.summary: Replace the TMS's copy of a Rate Card with the ERP's record.
put.description: Upserts the whole Rate Card, so a new one appears, and replaces its list of dated versions. Idempotent on the Master-data revision: a revision that is not higher than the copy's answers 200 with applied false and changes nothing. A replaced Rate Card changes only what is rated after it arrives. A record the TMS can't read is refused with 400 and the code MasterDataUnreadable; versions that overlap in time with RateCardVersionsOverlap.

put.summary: Replace the TMS's copy of a Carrier Rate Card with the ERP's record.
put.description: Upserts the whole Carrier Rate Card, so a new one appears, and replaces its list of dated versions. Idempotent on the Master-data revision: a revision that is not higher than the copy's answers 200 with applied false and changes nothing. A record the TMS can't read is refused with 400 and the code MasterDataUnreadable; versions that overlap in time with RateCardVersionsOverlap.

get.summary: Whether a reset would be taken now.
get.description: enabled is the Reset setting, which is off unless the estate switches it on. busySubscription names the first topic subscription that holds unprocessed messages, as topic/subscription, or is null when all are empty.

post.summary: Delete the TMS's transactional records and put the seed file's Rosters back in force.
post.description: Deletes the Transport Orders and everything hanging off them (Shipments, Trips, Exceptions, Carrier bookings, Tracking events, Proof of delivery records and files, Shipper notifications and outbox Messages) and the Planner's changes to Rosters, Absences and Off the road days (the open Planning days they shaped are opened again from the seed file's Rosters), and restarts the number sequences. Rate Cards, Carriers, Vehicles, Drivers and Shippers are reference data and stay. Refused, deleting nothing, with a 403 problem (code ResetDisabled) while the setting is off, and a 409 problem (code SubscriptionBusy) naming the subscription while one holds unprocessed messages.

get.summary: List the faults this application owns, with whether each is on and how long it has left.

put.summary: Switch one of this application's faults on, for a duration after which it expires by itself, or off.
put.description: Only a caller holding the app role Demo.Fault may call it. A duration longer than the application allows (a few minutes by default) is refused with 400.
